key_insight: Matching electronic descriptor body order to quantum-gate locality creates a physically interpretable encoding hierarchy that improves quantum machine-learning predictions of electron-correlation energies.
engineering_relevance: The approach guides quantum feature-map design using mean-field electronic data, with lower-order information offering an inexpensive route to higher-body encodings.
method: Extract electronic descriptors from a single mean-field electronic-structure calculation.
Map n-body descriptors to n-qubit gates, constructing one- through four-body encodings.
Compare reduced-density-matrix encodings, including disconnected many-particle densities built from lower-order information.
evidence_signal: On bond-stretching potential energy surfaces, higher-body encodings systematically improved accuracy toward the full configuration interaction limit, while disconnected densities matched explicitly correlated two-particle densities in key cases.
watch_item: Higher-body gates may require costly hardware decompositions; the abstract does not establish performance under device noise or beyond the tested bond-stretching benchmarks.
paper_title: Electronic-Structure-Informed Many-Body Encoding for Quantum Machine Learning
